title: Knowledge check: Typed Composables and Stores

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Typed Composables and Stores”?
options: Type annotations automatically validate HTTP response objects at runtime.
Every Vue 3 application must use TypeScript.
A type checker replaces browser and component tests.
Static types improve development-time contracts, while untrusted runtime data still needs validation.
questions.answer_key: Static types improve development-time contracts, while untrusted runtime data still needs validation.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Typed Composables and Stores directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Designing reusable typed functions”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Every Vue 3 application must use TypeScript.
A type checker replaces browser and component tests.
Static types improve development-time contracts, while untrusted runtime data still needs validation.
Type annotations automatically validate HTTP response objects at runtime.
questions.answer_key: Static types improve development-time contracts, while untrusted runtime data still needs validation.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Designing reusable typed functions”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Typed Composables and Stores” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
